open_questions: Q1. Does “Open the whole model” come in slice 2 or slice 3? Recommended: slice 3. What the switch keeps is standing freezes (FROZEN), and model-wide changes bring Proof broken, remove-arrow and FZ-5 meaning-changed items. The checks are already parameterised by Opening and the backstop has a held hook, so slice 3 only adds openings.

Q2. Does “Claude may add cards” (intermediate targets) come in slice 2? Recommended: slice 3. New PROPOSITION blocks written by Claude need new ledger and G5 exceptions and per-card targets inside one step. In slice 2, intermediate steps stay lemmas, as proof material of the Result.

Q3. How does Claude add an arrow? Recommended: a new tool, propose_arrow {source, target, why}. telelean validates it (proposeArrowProblems, with exact texts) and writes it into the working copy as a ledger 'arrow' entry. The alternative is Claude editing premises: directly. The tool keeps G5's rule that the agent never edits premises:/follows_from:, makes every arrow attributable, and gives immediate refusals.

Q4. May Claude add a Prop-valued axiom bound to no card (an unmarked axiom) as a belief item? Recommended: no. Refuse it with new-axiom, as today; it must be an Add premise card (S9: no hidden assumptions). RV-7's “unmarked axiom” then covers only changes to the user's existing ones, which needs whole-model mode (slice 3).

Q5. Must every changed declaration belong to an accepted item, including unreached lemmas and definitions that Appendix B exempts from the own-Accept rule? Recommended: yes. This is stricter than Appendix B: nothing unreviewed reaches the files, and a declined item's leftovers are caught.

Q6. May the user Accept a Result that is still hidden? Recommended: no. Disable it with “Decide its statements first, or press Show result”, and have group Accept leave hidden Results and their hidden parts. Otherwise a proof could be accepted unseen, and the blocker list would leak the hidden arrow items.

Q7. When does an accepted item return to in-review because its class changed? Recommended: whenever its badge set gains a member (belief or changes-what-is-proved going from false to true), not only when a group-accepted item becomes RV-7. The user accepted it under the old badges.

Q8. Proof-only declarations used by no Result (dangling): hidden or shown? Recommended: hidden while the Result of the step that created them is hidden (ownership by creating step, ledger 'created'). Showing them could hint at a failed attempt.

Q9. When F differs from the last judged state, which G4 checks rerun at Apply? Recommended: rerun freeze and comparator only for inferences whose proof's reach (uses mode) contains a declaration that differs between the last judged state and F; the others reuse their pass. The alternative, always rerunning every inference, costs N comparator jobs. The backstop and the pure checks always run.

Q10. What happens with facts that lack typeConsts (old recordings, a failed or fallback probe)? Recommended: classify conservatively (every new or changed definition or instance is belief), over-approximate dependencies (refs ∪ valueConsts), and refuse Apply (backstop 'facts') until a fresh build provides the arrays.

Q11. How are cycles among item dependencies handled (for example, two Results using each other's lemmas after a redo step)? Recommended: SCC treatment. Edges inside an SCC do not block Accept; members show “accepted together with …”; a decline inside the SCC makes the others to be redone; the backstop requires an SCC with any accepted member to be fully accepted.

Q12. Is a Result that proves an unproved or pending target (no theorem in B, statement unchanged) an RV-7 item? Recommended: no, per RV-7's letter and CF-2 (pending counts as no proof). It can be group-accepted once revealed and its dependencies are accepted. Results marked “replaces your proof” or “proves a statement changed in this session” are RV-7.

Q13. Can a mid-stage Formalize use Claude's arrows as its question? Recommended: only accepted ones, which “become yours” (§14.2). Arrows still in review are not selectable (“Accept this arrow first”), so Q(T) ⊆ arrows of B ∪ accepted Claude arrows.

Q14. DO-1 restores the previous version “at once”: is the restored working copy judged? Recommended: yes. Build and judge it in the background (judgeState 'stage', classes, dependency graph, hidden set, masked graph). Accept, Submit and Apply wait for that judgement, and the board shows “checking…” meanwhile.

Q15. How is the meaning of declarations a step did not open compared? Recommended: compare the valueConsts and typeConsts sets as well as the printed type and value, because printed values hide instance arguments. Full term comparison exists only in G4. Content keys use the same data.

Q16. Does R_stmt include the statements of Add premise items still in review (from their scratch facts)? Recommended: yes, so a definition such a premise relies on is classified belief before the premise is written.

Q17. May Claude propose an arrow from a card that has neither a proof nor a claim? Recommended: refuse with “‹card› has no proof and no claim: the proof cannot use it”, since B.1 gives such a source nothing.

Q18. Should evaluateRules be kept as a single-inference adapter over judgeState? Recommended: yes, so the M2 and 1e gate suites keep guarding every rule. The old single-target run path can be removed once sessions replace runs, in slice 2's integration.

Q19. Where are the masked RV-6 graphs computed? Recommended: in the extension host or runner, which has the facts, whenever the hidden set changes. The webview receives only masked graphs plus the list of hidden Result targets, never unmasked derived data while a Result is hidden.
safety_notes: I1, files only via a fully checked Apply. The final state F gets facts from a build of exactly F (filesKey); judgeState('final') and applyBackstop always run, with ownership re-derived B→F. Tested in session.apply.test.ts (a spy shows the backstop is never reused) and in backstop.test.ts.

I2, accepted means exact content. SessionItemRecord.accepted.key is checked against itemContentKey(F). A stale Undo, a reload, or a later step that changed accepted content cannot slip through. Tested: content-changed refusal; reload recomputation sends a mismatched item back to in-review.

Own-Accept backstop (Appendix B a/b/c): new or changed Lean axioms (except shape-passing sorts and predicates), definitions, instances and coercions in R_stmt(F), and existing names whose kind, type or value changed all need how='own'. RV-7 is recomputed on F. Tested with group-accepted belief items and with S5/S6 scenarios.

B.1 is never widened by Claude. A footprint enters permitted(T) only from the user's own unchanged proof from B, or from a session Result that passes its own inference in the same state, computed sources first. Tested: the P2-style cheat; a non-passing source Result is unusable.

B.2 holds on every judged state, per inference, with allowed = sources(Q(T) ∪ E(T)) and the cross-check, from elaborated facts only (source-only refuses). At Apply it is also checked for every proposition whose proof or Dependencies changed. Tested in the S14 scenarios, including the @[simp]/instance case with real Lean once.

The ES-2 preset is slice 2's S1/S15 protection. Everything existing at step start keeps its text and its meaning (printed type and value plus the valueConsts and typeConsts sets), except the openings: the target's proof (never removed or made an axiom), empty statements at the selected arrows' ends, and arrows into the target. Tested in the S1 scenarios, including a meaning change with unchanged text.

The B.3 and B.4 and CF-3 checks rely on a telelean ledger kept outside Claude's working copy. Claude never edits premises:/follows_from:/type:, never writes a .holds axiom for a proposition, and never adds arrows into axioms or non-targets. Pending→proved is only axiom→theorem with an identical type. Tested in S6, S15 and S18.
The baseline for G0 and new-axiom is always B. Content Claude wrote in earlier steps never counts as the user's text; new-axiom compares name AND type against B, which closes S6's name-reuse hole.

RV-6 non-interference: everything shown while a Result is hidden comes from the masked model (the .holds as at step start, proof-only declarations dropped, footprints recomputed). The property test requires byte-identical view data for proved versus not-proved working copies. This also fixes an existing 1d leak (webview/src/model/run.ts:672-675): a downstream card gets the “result hidden” chip only when the target's proof changed its status.

Another leak channel to cover in the same non-interference test: the run panel's live activity and notices, for example a gate entry for finish(proved). They must not reveal a hidden Result's outcome; the UI and session designers must sanitise or withhold them while the Result is hidden.

RV-5 makes the accepted items a self-contained whole at Apply: Accept is enabled only when dependencies outside the SCC are accepted, nothing is accepted as a side effect, every non-trivial SCC must be fully accepted, and decline cascades make dependents to be redone. Tested in dependencies.test.ts and the S4 scenarios.

Fail closed on missing elaborated facts: closures report complete:false, classification treats items as belief, dependencies over-approximate, the gate refuses B.2 as source-only, and the backstop refuses Apply with 'facts'.

The base never moves (ES-7, S22). The live watcher and the atomic plan-drift refusal disable Apply; sessions never create an accept-base commit, and the unreachable D-21 rebase is removed. Tested in session.apply.test.ts.

Exact repeats are refused as gate findings that count as attempts: DO-1 by content key against rejectedKeys, DO-3 as an identical Shaky set. Reworded repeats come back as the same item marked updated (S13: not a safety issue, because nothing enters without Accept).
A cycle of arrows already in B never counts as Claude's failed attempt (AP-13). Every judged state, and Apply, requires the drawn and solid arrow graph to be acyclic (§14.9).

Testing constraints: no real Claude (FakeBackend only, TELELEAN_NO_REAL_CLAUDE=1); never build into packages/extension/dist; vitest with one worker under capped.sh; real-Lean probe tests only above the 12 GB free-RAM gate, otherwise listed as not run.
